idiom_name: class delegation (`class Envelope(letter: Letter) : Letter by letter`)
implementation_notes: Kotlin implements the delegation natively: in `class Envelope(l: Letter) : Letter by l` the compiler generates an override for every member of Letter that forwards to the delegate, which it stores in a private I$delegate field during construction - so no stub methods are written at all. An override declared in the envelope replaces just that member while the others stay delegated. The delegation is bound once, at construction: the delegate expression is evaluated exactly once even if a mutable property was passed, so an envelope whose letter must be swapped at run time uses a var property plus explicit forwarding. The classic hand-written envelope is still justified when individual calls must be intercepted or when the letter changes while the object lives.
pitfalls: The delegate is captured once at construction (the spec's I$delegate field): passing a var and mutating it later does not change what the delegated methods call, so runtime swapping needs explicit overrides.

Delegated members are copied from the interface at compile time, so adding a member to Letter forces the delegating class to be recompiled - which matters for a published library, even though the source needs no edit.

Overrides in the envelope are invisible to the delegate: the delegate's own implementations can only call themselves, so template-method-style chains through the envelope silently bypass the override.
